Subject: Q3 capacity needs & renewal conversation

Hi Grace,

Hope you're well — we're starting planning for our Q3 feature ramp and wanted to flag that our hosted usage has been trending up faster than expected. Attached is a tight export of our monthly usage for Q1 so you can see the spike in peak minutes and token counts.

Short version: we expect a ~2.5x increase in peak traffic across our checkout personalization endpoints by July, and the current rate limits have started to generate 429s at peak. We'd like to discuss bumping our monthly commitment and adjusting the throttling profile so our engineers aren't firefighting on release days.

Can you share what options you have for a short-term uplift versus a longer-term commit change? Procurement will want term/price detail — I'm looping Jasper and the procurement alias to keep them in the loop.

Attachment: AeroRetail_Monthly_Usage_Q1.csv

Hi Maya — thanks for the data, that helps.

On Tue, Feb 24, 2026 at 9:12 AM Maya Singh <maya.singh@aeroretail.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Hope you're well — we're starting planning for our Q3 feature ramp...
> (see attached)

We can support the uplift in a couple of ways:
- Short-term: temporary capacity uplift for 3 months (no long-term commit) — increases base rate limits and burst throttles, billed at a higher unit price.
- Committed uplift: increase monthly token commitment with a lower unit price and a higher baseline throughput (recommended if this trend continues).

Based on the usage file, a conservative recommend is moving AeroRetail to a 2,000,000 tokens/month committed tier (current is 800k) with an elevated baseline throttling profile: baseline request limit increase to 600 req/s with a burst allowance up to 1,800 req/s for short spikes. That should eliminate 429s for your observed bursts while keeping latency SLOs intact.

I've attached a high-level rate card that maps those tiers to pricing and rollback windows — see proposed-ratecard-v2.pdf. If procurement wants a 12-month term we can show a blended price with preferred discounts.

Next steps:
1) If you prefer the committed uplift, confirm target committed tokens and term length (6 vs 12 months).
2) We'll generate an amendment (redline) and a DocuSign link for approval.
3) Ben (cc'd) can run a quick runway test to help size an autoscaling buffer and minimize cold-start latency.

Would you have 30 minutes tomorrow or Thursday to align?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity needs & renewal conversation — technical sizing notes

Hey team — adding a few technical points that will affect the final amendment and recommended tier.

- Based on the usage export, your 99th percentile concurrent requests map to ~1,200 req/s during peak windows. To avoid queuing we should size the baseline to cover sustained 75% of that (approx. 900 req/s) and allow bursts to ~1,800 req/s. That aligns with Grace's recommended 600->1,800 profile; the difference is we suggest autoscale headroom for scheduled marketing spikes.
- If you opt for a committed uplift, we can enable prefix/KV caching for the personalization endpoints which will reduce effective token usage by ~15-25% (depends on prompt stability). That reduces billable tokens and improves tail latency.
- For customers on hosted plans hitting higher throughput, we sometimes recommend a soft isolation (dedicated pool) rather than full dedicated capacity — lower cost and quicker to provision. Grid can be provisioned in 48–72 hours once amendment is signed.

I've attached a short runbook I'll follow during the runway test and a pointer to our batching/caching recommendations: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/abcdefg

If procurement needs sample language for the amendment (SLA: latency targets, rollback windows), Grace — I left suggested clauses in the redline template I'll share with you after this thread.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement reviewed the numbers and is comfortable proceeding with the committed uplift if we can get the following in the amendment:
- 12-month term starting May 1, 2026
- Monthly committed tokens: 2,000,000
- Baseline request throughput: 600 req/s with burst to 1,800 req/s; clear rollback clause if sustained >90% of baseline for more than 14 days
- Clarity on invoicing cadence (monthly) and PO acceptance details (we'll attach a PO once we have the amendment)

Procurement contact: procurement@aeroretail.com (PO team). Billing: jasper.lin@aeroretail.com.

If you can send a redline and DocuSign link by Wednesday, procurement will route the PO same day.

—Maya
